newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steadies after record-low fall on float.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steadies after record-low fall on float.

text.p: The Thai baht was steadier at 0600 GMT after an initial plunge to a record low following news the Bank of Thailand had floated the currency on Wednesday morning, dealers said.
The flotation effectively devalued the baht by between 15-20 percent as the central bank dropped its pegged rate system against a basket of currencies and allowed market forces to set exchange rates.
Earlier, the baht tumbled to a traded low of around 29.00 and an indicated low of 29.25 at which there was no trades.

The baht was trading at 27.00/29.00 on onshore markets, unchanged for two hours. Trade was quiet as uncertainty surrounded the natural value of the baht and central bank's statement that it would set a daily reference rate and it had a certain level in mind to intervene, dealers said.

The central bank said earlier it would set a reference rate for the baht based on the previous day's trades. But it also said it had an "appropriate rate" for the currency, and stated it would intervene to defend it as part of the managed float.
"Trade is fairly quiet as we really don't know what is going to happen. Everyone seems afraid to set a level," said a trader at a major local bank.
The offshore market was also quiet as dealers struggled to discern a baht/dollar level. The baht was quoted at 28.00/29.00 per dollar in the offshore markets, dealers said.
